thread:
maria: Quick design review — prototype for the playground output controls. want feedback on streaming UI, stop/regenerate affordance, token counter placement, and how prompt snippets slot into the composer. screenshot + prototype link: https://figma.redwood/mock

owen: skimmed the figma. overall like the compact rail but a few questions: is ‘stop’ destructive? does it keep partial response for edit or always discard?

alex: good q. current idea: Stop = halts stream but keeps partial text. Regenerate will re-run same prompt. Pause would be visual-only (hold stream) but still cost tokens, so we avoided that term.

jia: prefer "Pause" for users who expect to freeze but keep token flow visible. we can show an explicit label: "Stop (keeps partial)" vs "Regenerate" to reduce confusion.

sam: small UX nit: Stop button feels heavy on the right rail. can we try an inline micro-control next to the message bubble? like a 24px icon button that appears on hover/focus.

maria: yes — two variants in figma: rail-control and inline micro. can we A/B test? rail is easier for keyboard discovery though.

owen: keyboard accessibility: primary keys should be Cmd/Ctrl+Enter for send, Esc to stop stream, and Ctrl+R to regenerate. need aria-live region for streaming so screen readers announce new tokens only when chunk ends.

alex: aria suggestion: use <div role=\"status\" aria-live=\"polite\" aria-atomic=\"false\"> for stream container. when stream completes flip aria-atomic to true so SR reads final summary.

jia: also token counter placement — current mock has it under the input. i think a subtle inline token ledger above the prompt area is better (less jumpy). show per-turn tokens and total session tokens on hover.

sam: can we show a small burn animation? not necessary for MVP but helpful for new users. also add tooltip: "Tokens estimate includes cached prefixes".

maria: copy options — short list: "Stop generation" vs "Pause" vs "Halt". which is clearest?

owen: vote: "Stop" + small helper text "keeps partial output". keep verbs imperative. :+1:

alex: agree. "Stop generation" for clarity. and a fallback toast: "Generation stopped — partial response saved" with undo option.

jia: prompt library integration: allow dragging a snippet into composer, preview tokens cost on hover, and a pin to mark favorites. maybe a collapsed shelf at left that expands on focus.

sam: dev note: drag-and-drop is medium complexity but copy/paste import is quick win. also need to surface model/temperature presets per snippet.

maria: ok roadmap: MVP = inline micro stop, aria-live stream, token counter above input (collapsed), prompt shelf collapsed + paste support. Followups = drag/drop, animations, A/B for rail vs inline.

design-bot: Prototype updated with inline stop variant and aria notes: https://figma.redwood/mock/v2 — pinned to project board.

owen: i can add front-end PR with aria changes and Esc handler. tagging @alex for backend token accounting adjustments.

alex: noted. will add per-turn token API + estimate flag. will mock sample response: ```json
{
  "tokens": { "input": 45, "output_so_far": 23, "estimate_total": 120 }
}
```

maria: sweet. can we aim to ship a dogfood build to internal users next week? small flag rollout and telemetry for stop/regenerate events.

sam: i’ll add telemetry events: playground.generate.start, playground.generate.stop, playground.generate.regenerate, playground.tokens.displayed. include reason tag for stop (user, timeout, error).

jia: accessibility checklist: keyboard focus for inline control, aria-live implementation, readable color contrast for token badge (AA), focus ring visible on high-contrast mode.

maria: perfect. thanks all — will consolidate notes into the spec doc and update the figma with final labels. :rocket:
